title: Gitea's repositories and its generated app.ini have no backup at all
The R2 backups are not encrypted, and two documents say they are

comments.author: ZY-Ang
comments.body: /adhd please. I don't get your wall of text.

comments.author: ZY-Ang
comments.body:
🤖

Rewritten — the wall of text is gone. The whole thing is now:

**Pick A or B.**

- **A.** Scramble the backups. Safest, but adds a password that must never be lost — lose it and every backup is unreadable forever.
- **B.** Leave them, and I fix the two documents that wrongly claim they are already scrambled.

That is the entire decision. Everything else moved into a fold.

One thing worth knowing either way: the claim is false **today**. `AGENTS.md` and `docs/host-state.md` both say the storage "holds nothing but ciphertext", and only the vault's own backup is. I will correct that whichever you pick.

comments.author: ZY-Ang
comments.body:
🤖

Rewritten — it is now just A or B, and the rest is folded away.

On your question: **the Cloudflare dashboard cannot tell you this.** It may say objects are encrypted at rest, and that is true and irrelevant — it protects against someone stealing Cloudflare's disks, not against someone with your R2 token, who gets the file already decrypted.

The only check that answers it is reading a backup: a plain PostgreSQL dump starts with the letters `PGDMP`. The exact command is in the issue body.

I already know the answer from the config — no cipher in `pgbackrest.conf`, a plain `pg_dump -Fc` in the script — so run it only if you want to see it yourself.

**Still needs you:** you still have to pick A or B; the trade is yours, not mine

comments.author: ZY-Ang
comments.body: Need more details on the two available options, and the problem we are trying to solve

comments.author: ZY-Ang
comments.body:
🤖

Rewritten with the detail you asked for. The whole thing is now the problem in one paragraph, then each option with what it costs.

**The problem:** your database is copied to Cloudflare R2 daily and those copies are not scrambled. Anyone with the R2 key downloads and reads them directly — every Gitea password hash, every tenant row. The key lives on the NAS.

**A** — pgBackRest encrypts them. A stolen key becomes useless. The cost is a passphrase that can **never** be lost, stored off the NAS with your unseal keys; lose it and every backup is permanently unreadable, including the one you reach for in a disaster.

**B** — leave them. Nothing new to lose; the key stays the only thing protecting the database.

**I would pick B, narrowly** — a lost passphrase is a worse day than a leaked key, and the key is scoped to one bucket and rotatable in a click while the passphrase is neither. That flips if the key ever gets exposed more widely, or the database starts holding something you would mind being read.

I fix the two documents either way, because they currently claim the backups already are encrypted.

**Still needs you:** A or B — the trade between a leaked key and a lost passphrase is yours

title: Plan: what this platform cannot tell you about itself, and the order to fix it

gitea-init purges the admin on any non-2xx, and three of those causes are permanent
